strokeOrderSource.citation: Zer o Zabar, To’e, zo’e, se, zhe, and ġhain, independent ظ handwriting animation and Zo’e instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent handwriting animation draws the closed to'e-series body and leftward finish first, then adds the tall upright and the single dot above as separate marks. The adjacent prose identifies zo'e as to'e with one dot above and shows the same shape in every position. This learner path fits that body-first, two-lift order to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. The provenance remains Urdu-specific rather than borrowing the separate Persian or Arabic ظ sources.

notes: Zo'e appears mainly in Arabic-derived words and is pronounced z in Urdu.
